source.title: A Constructive Prediction of the Generalization Error Across Scales
source.authors: Jonathan S. Rosenfeld; Amir Rosenfeld; Yonatan Belinkov; N. Shavit

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error while scaling model size, conceptually bearing on width and generalization, but does not test the specific one-hidden-layer ReLU interpolation-threshold setup in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error landscapes over model and data scales. Optimizer/architecture fit-quality comparisons and cited prior-work results are not rows because they do not report how the claim's generalization behavior changes.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out error as networks widen, but never establishes which widths achieve zero training error. It therefore cannot test V2's defining claim about widening beyond that threshold. Its fixed-budget, regularized training also differs from V2's convergence without explicit regularization. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose a joint model/data-size function that fits measured held-out-error landscapes and supports small-to-large-scale extrapolation. They qualify this by fixed hyperparameters and by extrapolation failures when small-scale measurements lack sufficient signal or configurations.
record.recipe_differences: Width/depth scaling of varied vision and language architectures with dataset size also varied; fixed hyperparameters. Not the one-hidden-layer ReLU interpolation-threshold setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error changes with model size and dataset size; the paper reports a renewed slight increase at large model size on UCF101.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the explored vision and language settings, held-out error generally decreases with width and then approaches a dataset-size-dependent plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under fixed training recipes, width scaling often produces diminishing held-out-error improvements; these measurements do not locate the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: On UCF101, the authors report a slight renewed test-error increase at larger model sizes without a corresponding training-error increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width scaling can produce overfitting under the tested fixed recipe, without establishing whether this occurs beyond zero training error.

record.problems: The study does not report training error or identify the interpolation threshold, so it cannot determine how results relate to widening past zero training error. Scale-specific values are principally in figures. Hyperparameters are held fixed.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant model-size/test-error landscape results left out; fit-quality and extrapolation-error results evaluate the approximation method rather than the claim's model-size/generalization behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Whether test error keeps falling when widening beyond the width achieving zero training error; convergence without explicit regularization and the specified one-hidden-layer classification settings.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Matched adaptive-versus-SGD held-out-performance comparisons under tuning constraints. Section 6.2 compares approximation quality, without reporting matched optimizer performance differences.
Batch-size interventions and their held-out-performance effects under fixed or adapted training budgets.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their association with generalization gaps.
Removal of highly memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V2 limits_scope labels. Missing evidence about the interpolation threshold is an untested prerequisite, not a demonstrated scope limitation. Appendix C gives a qualitative training-error comparison for UCF101, so the record's blanket statement that no training-error information is reported is too strong.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.

One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 conditions, training error and interpolation threshold; the paper studies other architectures and datasets and does not locate zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effect on test error.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.size_stated: 25.5M base parameters; width scales in Table 1
rows.operation_detail: Width scaling; test-error landscape measured across model and data scales.
rows.measure: Top-1 test error across model scales
rows.note: The paper says model scaling initially decreases error and then saturates; the plots provide the scale-specific measurements.
rows.check: ImageNet width-scaling results do not identify zero training error or establish a post-interpolation regime. Training uses weight decay and a fixed 90-epoch budget; saturation cannot establish a limitation of V2.
